labs.title: Project 00, the counterexample lab

stages.title: Run the Z3Py introductory example, then the roadmap's starter; see `sat`, then `unsat`
stages.what: Run the Z3Py introductory example, then the roadmap's starter, and see the answer change when the guard arrives. Call the two answers first. The starter prints its own answer, so this call is practice and is never scored.

checks.label: The answer pair reproduces.
checks.passes: `z3.get_version_string()` reports the pinned version, and `starter.py` prints a model and then `unsat` {{run:RUN-z3-starter}}. Model values are not compared. The introductory example is run and logged, not graded.

stages.title: Find a transfer that makes the source balance negative
stages.what: Find a transfer that makes the source balance negative. Then minimize your witness's amount with Optimize, and say what "minimal" covers.

checks.label: Your violation query finds a real overdraft.
checks.passes: Your violation query has a model, and that model satisfies `a >= 0`, `b >= 0` and `amount > 0` and leaves the sender below zero under your encoding. Reported but not required: whether your query is equivalent to the premises plus the negated property. A narrower query gets a distinguishing state, "your query would miss this violation".

stages.title: Add the sufficient-funds guard: `unsat`, plus a satisfiable premise witness
stages.what: Add the sufficient-funds guard. The violation query should then have no model, and a premise query beside it should have one. Then drop `amount > 0` and predict the sender's answer over `Int`.

checks.label: The guard works, and its answer is not empty.
checks.passes: The guarded violation query has no model. The premise query, with the premises and the guard and no negated property, has a model that satisfies every premise. The guard is equivalent to `amount <= a` under the premises, so a guard that also rejects a full-balance transfer fails with the state that shows it. The violation query is equivalent to the premises plus the guard plus the negated property, so extra constraints cannot make "no model" cheap.

stages.title: Introduce the buggy refund rule, find the second counterexample, fix it so a non-minimal witness also dies
stages.what: Introduce the buggy refund rule and find the second counterexample. Fix it so that a witness you have not seen dies too. Then find which conjunct of your fixed refund is load-bearing by deleting each in turn.

checks.label: The fix kills the whole class.
checks.passes: Your mint query on `broken/refund.py` has a model that replays, and the witness is written to your specimens. Your mint query on `fixed/refund.py` has no model for the base parameters, and for two parameter sets drawn at grade time from the bug's family: a non-zero floor, a prior partial refund, a fee. The fixed rule's premise query has a model, so some refund with `r > 0` is accepted, because rejecting every refund is not a fix. A non-minimal witness of the clamp class, drawn at grade time, is rejected or conserves under your fixed rule.

stages.title: Conservation and double capture as two-state properties
stages.what: Write conservation and the double capture as two-state properties, with primed variables. Then ask whether conservation catches your double capture.

checks.label: Both properties give the expected answers on fresh seeds.
checks.passes: On the base model and on three seeds drawn at grade time (hold amounts, other holds pooled in `held`, initial status): the transfer step, written with primed variables, conserves the total (the negation has no model) and the step relation itself has a model. The buggy capture applied twice has a model for the at-most-once query, with a witness that replays. The fixed capture has none. One fixed capture succeeds.

stages.title: README with the property, assumptions, solver answer, example model and limitations; two claim cards prefilled from the receipt
stages.what: Write the README with the property, assumptions, solver answer, example model and limitations. Two claim cards are prefilled from your receipt.

checks.label: The README matches the receipt, and the cards hold.
checks.passes: The README has the headings Property, Assumptions, Solver answer, Example model and Limitations, each non-empty. Every answer line under Solver answer matches a receipt line word for word, with the solver version and the budget. The example model replays as a violation of the stated property. Both cards (CL-1.1 and CL-1.4) pass the claim check: six fields present, method, tool and version equal to the receipt's, the statement hash equal to the hash of your `claims/*.smt2` file, the "if weakened" witness refuting the claim's own proposition on replay, and requirement-fit never marked [P]. Prose quality is not graded, and nothing here is graded by a language model.

labs.summary: Project 00 is the roadmap's first-weekend checklist plus conservation and a double capture. It runs on your machine with `uv run`, pinned to the same solver version as the tab (5.3.1), or entirely in the tab. It never needs a devcontainer. Each stage ends in a check that reads the solver's answer, and a model is graded by replaying it, never by matching its values. Every stage opens with a call: predict, then run the reference.

stages.title: Run the reference checker on the guarded Transfer: "proved for the fragment" plus a premise witness

checks.label: The reference output, reproduced
checks.passes: The verdict is `unsat`, the stamp names the solver, its version, the word uncertified and the `rlimit`, and the premise witness satisfies `Inv ∧ Guard ∧ Step` and replays as a successful step. {{run:RUN-check-fragment}} The witness is checked by running it, never by matching its values.

stages.title: Weakest precondition of assignment emitted as SMT-LIB
stages.what: Write `wp_emit`: the weakest precondition of an assignment or a ResourceOp, as SMT-LIB. The seeds include aliasing and capture-prone commands.

checks.label: Weakest preconditions match the reference
checks.passes: On 20 fresh seeds of assignment shapes, aliasing and capture-prone seeds included, your output is Z3-equivalent to the reference on every seed. A failing seed shows the state where the two disagree. A seed Z3 cannot decide is drawn again and counted, and each seed's `rlimit` is printed.

stages.title: Conditionals and guards
stages.what: Extend `wp_emit` to sequences, conditionals and guards, with all four readings of a guard. Name the intermediate formulas so that a chain of conditionals stays small.

stages.what: Write `vc_emit` with its forward route: `Inv ∧ Guard ∧ Step ∧ ¬Inv′`, with a named frame for every account the command leaves alone.

checks.label: Frames are stated, and every one is needed
checks.passes: First, on 20 fresh obligations over at least three accounts that are known to hold, the forward route reports a proved obligation with a premise witness that replays. Second, every `frame_<k>` is load-bearing: deleting it turns `unsat` into `sat`, with account k changing. Third, the two routes agree on every seed.

stages.title: Capstone S10.L3: decode models into Mini-Plinth states and replay them in the interpreter
stages.what: Capstone S10.L3. Write `model_decode`: turn a Z3 model into a Mini-Plinth state and replay it in the interpreter. A model that does not replay is a defect in your generator, never a finding about the command.

checks.label: Every refutation replays
checks.passes: On the fixtures and 10 fresh seeds, every REFUTED result decodes into a state that the interpreter replays to the same violation, and every premise witness replays as a success. stages.title: CTI or reachable: output "inductive", "CTI", "REACHABLE in k" or "none within N"

checks.label: Verdicts match the reference

stages.title: Miscompile your own checker by over-constraining the translation (a guard strengthened in translation, a dropped effect or an over-broad frame) so that a known-false obligation reports [P]; locate the faulty translation; keep it in `broken/` (the roadmap's adversarial exercise; a dropped frame conjunct only turns `unsat` into a false alarm, never a [P])
stages.what: Break your own checker on purpose. Miscompile one construct so that a known-false obligation is reported proved, find the faulty translation, and keep the broken build in `broken/`. Dropping a frame conjunct is not enough, because it only gives a false alarm. Over-constrain instead: strengthen a guard, drop an effect or widen a frame.

checks.label: A false proof, located and fixed
checks.passes: One: `broken/` reports PROVED on a fixture whose reference verdict is REFUTED, through a strengthened guard, a dropped effect or an over-broad frame. Two: its premise-witness status is recorded, `sat` for a proof that is not vacuous and `unsat` for one that is. Three: `fixed/` reports REFUTED with a witness that replays. Four: fixture and semantics hashes match across builds. Five: reverting the hunk tagged `MISCOMPILE` restores REFUTED, so locating the bug is graded.

checks.passes: cvc5 and Z3 agree on every authored `unsat` in your fixtures and claims, and a disagreement fails the check. CL-4.2 and CL-4.4 or CL-4.5 pass claim validation, their statement hashes match the receipt, and each "if weakened" witness refutes its own proposition.

labs.summary: Build `miniplinth check`, a checker for Mini-Plinth commands. It reads a command and an invariant, emits an SMT-LIB obligation, asks Z3, decodes a model into a state and replays it in the interpreter, and reports a stamp with its premise witness. The first stage runs the reference checker so you see the output before you write any. Stages 2 to 7 are your Rust, compiled to wasm and graded in the tab on seeds drawn at grade time. Stage 8 runs on your machine and compares Z3 with cvc5. This lab builds capstone step S10.L3.

extra.grading: LAB-4.1 runs the reference module in the tab and earns nothing. LAB-4.2 to LAB-4.7 run your Rust compiled to wasm in the tab and are graded on seeds drawn at grade time (badge: re-checked here); each check runs in a fresh instance of your module. LAB-4.8 and LAB-4.9 run on your machine (badge: reported from your machine).
extra.template: The template supplies the reader for the command format, the vocabulary, the output format, the fragment declaration, the host and the fixtures: known-true and known-false obligations, the third-account fee fixture, the off-by-one Withdraw and the capture-prone postconditions. You write the weakest-precondition emitter, the forward step with its frames, the model decoder, the CTI driver, a miscompile and its fix, and the claim cards.

contract.exports: wp_emit, vc_emit (route `wp` or `forward`), model_decode, bmc_emit(system, inv, k), verdict_compose
contract.vocabulary: State symbols come from the command format. The post-state suffix is `_p`, and parameters are `p_<name>`. The obligation is one `assert`, shared through `let` and `define-fun`, with no extra `declare-const`, so equivalence with the reference is quantifier-free over a fixed vocabulary.
contract.outputLines: command, fragment, query (SHA-256), solver (version, `rlimit`, entry path), verdict, premise, stamp, defeaters

hints.gate: Every ladder opens with an explanation gate: write a teach-back of the failing check (what it tested, the invariant, your hypothesis), then reveal three authored ideas and tick the ones you covered. It is self-assessed and never credited. R1 opens after a teach-back of at least 12 words. Work past R2 is credited as assisted until an unseen variant passes.

ladders.r1: A premise witness shows that the premises can hold together.
ladders.r4: An `unsat` on its own may be vacuous.

ladders.r1: A weakest precondition is substitution, and ResourceOps substitute sequential updates.
ladders.r2: Look at `subst` on `forall`, and at the order of the two updates in `move`.

SQLSTATEs come from the server's csv log: each session's application_name is '<tag>/<session>', and for every session the messages the tester printed must equal the messages the server logged, in order; a mismatch stops the run.
NULL prints as an empty cell in isolationtester output; an empty string prints the same way.

A session that continues after an error meets 'current transaction is aborted' (25P02) at its next write. Those follow-on errors stay in the row outputs, as after_abort in the index, and keep a history out of the GEN-anomaly-id pool.
The lock model that decides which interleavings cannot hang the tester is sound and incomplete; every lock wait the tester reported was one the model predicted.
